key.name: show-firefox-family
key.description: Include Firefox, Zen, LibreWolf, Floorp and related browsers in the menu.

key.name: show-chrome-family
key.description: Include Chromium, Chrome, Edge, Brave, Falkon and related browsers in the menu.

key.name: show-simple-browsers
key.summary: Show profile-less browsers in the Browsers row
key.description: Include profile-less browsers (GNOME Web, qutebrowser, …) as single icons in the "Browsers" row. Independent of "show-profiled-browsers" below — the "Browsers" row itself stays visible as long as either setting is on.

key.name: show-profiled-browsers
key.summary: Show profile-based browsers in the Browsers row
key.description: Also list Firefox/Chrome-family browsers (Firefox, Chromium, Brave, Falkon, …) as single icons in the "Browsers" row, in addition to their own detailed section above. Independent of "show-simple-browsers" above.

key.name: show-single-profile-detail
key.description: By default, a Firefox/Chrome-family browser with only one profile and no active spaces/workspaces has its one-item detailed section hidden and is shown only in the "Browsers" row; turning this on keeps its detailed section too. Independent of "show-profiled-browsers".

key.name: firefox-profile-groups-mode
key.description: How to display Firefox Profile Groups (Firefox 128+, separate from the classic Profile Manager). "spaces": show as space buttons under the matched profile entry. "profiles": list each selectable profile as its own menu entry. "off": ignore them entirely.

key.name: show-zen-workspaces
key.description: Display workspace buttons under each Zen Browser profile entry.

key.name: show-toolbar
key.description: Show the top row: the default browser quick-launch button, its edit pencil, Refresh, and Settings. Turning this off hides all four — Settings will then need to be reached another way (e.g. the GNOME Extensions app).

key.name: show-default-browser-edit
key.description: Sub-setting of "show-toolbar" (has no effect when that is off). Display the pencil button next to the default browser name that opens Default Applications settings.

key.name: show-default-browser-panel-icon
key.summary: Show the default browser's own icon in the panel
key.description: Use the resolved default browser's own icon in the top panel instead of the generic web-browser-symbolic icon. Falls back to the generic icon when no default browser is detected or its icon can't be resolved.
